question: A 2-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a 3-minute episode of a tonic-clonic seizure. The parents deny any previous history of seizure involving the patient or the family. Physical examination reveals an afebrile, well-groomed, and playful appearance, with normal vital signs. The patient carries a pink birthmark on the right side of her face extending from the forehead to the zygomatic arch. Which of the following findings is most likely on a head CT of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pink birthmark on right side of face" -> "Possible Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "Leptomeningeal angioma associated with Sturge-Weber" -> "Prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Tonic-clonic seizure" -> "Potential underlying brain abnormality" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome due to facial port-wine stain" -> "Leptomeningeal capillary-venous malformations" -> "Prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 75%

CHAIN: "2-year-old with first seizure" -> "No fever or systemic symptoms" -> "Structural brain lesion possible" -> "Facial port-wine stain suggests neurocutaneous syndrome" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome likely" -> "Prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification typical in Sturge-Weber" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Seizure in toddler" -> "Normal physical and vital signs post-seizure" -> "Presence of facial birthmark" -> "Indicative of possible neurocutaneous disorder" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome associated with port-wine stain" -> "Prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification as common finding in Sturge-Weber" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Facial port-wine stain" -> "Suspect Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "Brain involvement in Sturge-Weber" -> "Calcification of cerebral cortex and white matter" -> "Prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification on CT" -> 75%
analysis: The description of the pink birthmark on the right side of the face extending from the forehead to the zygomatic arch suggests the possibility of Sturge-Weber syndrome, a neurocutaneous disorder. This syndrome is often associated with a port-wine stain facial birthmark and neurological abnormalities. One of the characteristic findings on imaging in patients with Sturge-Weber syndrome is leptomeningeal angioma, which can lead to calcifications in the affected cerebral cortex. Therefore, prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification is a likely finding on a head CT in this context.
